stem: A manufacturing study measures defect rate across 3 factorys, each containing multiple production lines. factory A has 10 observations with mean 38.0 % (within-factory SD = 9.8). factory B has 20 observations with mean 51.7 % (within-factory SD = 7.7). factory C has 8 observations with mean 27.2 % (within-factory SD = 5.9). The between-factory standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 8.3 and 20.9 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true defect rate for factory C, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-factory variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for factory C: 27.5 % (shrunk from raw 27.2). Range [27.4, 28.1] as between-factory SD varies from 8.3 to 20.9. Pooled mean: 42.9.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 42.9 % (weighted average of 3 factory means).
Shrinkage factor for factory C: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/8). At σ_between=13.9: B = 0.978.
Interval [27.4, 28.1] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (27.2) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (42.9) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
